title: Minimax Regret for Robust Policy Adoption across Multiple Sites
banked_reason: The repaired package is sound, but the final cold review grades it incremental with paper-score ceiling 6.0 below the 7.4 field floor; a feasible general nonparametric upper theorem remains project-sized.
gap_reasons: The data-only upper guarantee is confined to that fixed-support subexperiment, so the package does not yet establish a feasible frontier at general nonparametric centers.
The general finite-policy characterization adapts finite-prior minimax machinery already developed for a different loss in Joo's public preprint, rather than delivering a broadly usable new rule.
D0.5.G projected paper-score gate: paper_score_ceiling 6 < 7.4, so the graded tier 'subfield' is capped at 'incremental'.
proof_attempt_summary: The run certified the causally realized two-site minimum-adoption Gaussian value to a bracket narrower than 0.001, proved a strict unknown-binding penalty, and developed finite-policy Gaussian image and conditional full-law lower-transfer results. It also proved a cross-fitted data-only rule on explicit fixed-support Bernoulli paths, but the attempted general feasible transfer had to be narrowed because arbitrary attainable tangent directions need not be realized by full-law paths. Reaching the field floor would require a new locally uniform feasible theorem at regular nonparametric centers with estimated covariance, nuisance functions, centering, and unknown or rank-changing active sets.
tldr: The two-site adoption question is resolved to its stipulated \(0.001\) tolerance: at a causally realized policy and binding-site tie, an explicit Gaussian prior and smooth rule certify minimax regret between \(0.21438933\) and \(0.21534\). The cross-fitted implementation transfers this rule on fixed-support Bernoulli causal paths and recovers the revealed-binding constant on proved escaping gaps. A general finite-policy Gaussian game has an exact finite-prior characterization; causal lower transfer at a full-law center uses actual paths, while general feasible exact-frontier transfer remains open.
gap: Existing scalar treatment-choice minimax theory, coordinate-mean Gaussian selection, and multisite regret-rate work do not give the sharp simple-regret rule for a policy payoff that is a minimum of site gains. The exact unrestricted two-site adoption value remains unknown.
fill: Solve or tightly certify the smallest continuous Gaussian game, characterize representative finite-policy tangent geometries, and determine conditions under which cross-fitted efficient gains transfer that frontier to multisite causal data.
